supersedes: probes-2026-08-31.json, which used the wrong fire detector. See detectorCorrection.
detectorCorrection: The 2026-08-31 probes detected firing by whether the reply named the skill. That is wrong: the model uses a skill content without announcing it. The correct detector is the planted figures — 4.2 Nm, 90 seconds, 0.3 degrees — which appear only in the planted SKILL.md and cannot come from training data. The 2026-08-31 conclusions happen to survive, because the figure check was also negative there, but the reasoning was unsound and one condition below fires with the figures present and the name absent.
plantedSkill: zqx-handler, an uninformative name with a hydrofoil trim tab description and three invented figures in its body. Installed at .claude/skills/ in a scratch workspace.
fireCriterion: at least two of the three planted figures present in the reply
finding: The failure needs BOTH a large library AND a bare question. Shrinking the library rescues it (0/3 -> 3/3) and so does giving it a task-shaped prompt (0/3 -> 3/3). A stronger model helps a little and does not fix it (1/3).
measurementArtifactFound: The first sonnet run recorded 0/3. --max-budget-usd was set to 0.3 in the runner and a sonnet trial costs about 0.36, so the trials were truncated before answering. Re-run at 1.5 it is 1/3. A budget flag chosen for haiku silently produced a wrong number for a different model.
limits: n=3 per condition, one planted skill, one harness mode.
B changes which skills are installed as well as how many: --setting-sources project drops the plugin-provided skills rather than sampling 13 of the 44. Size and composition are confounded.
Every condition is claude -p. Whether interactive sessions behave the same is still untested and is the Q3 the sketch names as least automatable and most consequential.
A planted skill on an invented subject is the cleanest possible signal. A real skill competing with the model own knowledge of the subject is a harder case and is not measured here.
